prompt_rendered: What is the current annual mean ambient air quality standard for PM2.5 in Brazil, according to CONAMA Resolution 491/2018? Provide the value in µg/m³ and indicate whether it refers to the interim or final target. Limit answer to 1-3 sentences.
ground_truth: Brazil's current annual mean PM2.5 ambient air quality standard is 20 µg/m³ under Intermediate Target PI-1 (the standard in force in 2026), as established by CONAMA Resolution 491/2018. The Final Target is 10 µg/m³, aligned with the WHO 2005 guideline but not yet binding. Brazil has not yet adopted the WHO 2021 guideline of 5 µg/m³ annual.
ground_truth_source: Resolução CONAMA 491/2018: https://www.in.gov.br/materia/-/asset_publisher/Kujrw0TZC2Mb/content/id/55643907; WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228

prompt_rendered: According to the most recent annual report by CETESB (the São Paulo State Environmental Agency), what was the mean annual PM2.5 concentration in the São Paulo Metropolitan Region (RMSP) in 2023? Provide the value in µg/m³, the reference station(s), and the source.
ground_truth: Per CETESB's 'Relatório de Qualidade do Ar no Estado de São Paulo 2023' (published 2024), the annual mean PM2.5 in the RMSP was approximately 16–22 µg/m³ depending on station, with central stations such as Pinheiros and Congonhas reporting near the upper end. The state-wide annual mean in monitored RMSP stations was ~17 µg/m³, exceeding the WHO 2021 guideline (5 µg/m³) and approaching CONAMA PI-1 (20 µg/m³).
ground_truth_source: CETESB. Qualidade do Ar no Estado de São Paulo 2023. https://cetesb.sp.gov.br/ar/publicacoes-relatorios/; SISAM/MMA archive: https://sisam.mma.gov.br/

prompt_rendered: Summarize the epidemiological evidence on mortality attributable to ambient PM2.5 exposure in Brazil for the period 2015-2024. Include estimated annual deaths, primary causes (e.g., cardiovascular, respiratory), and at least one authoritative source.
ground_truth: GBD 2019 (IHME, published 2020) estimated approximately 50,000 deaths/year in Brazil attributable to ambient PM2.5 exposure, dominated by cardiovascular causes (ischemic heart disease, stroke) and lower respiratory infections. WHO Air Pollution and Health (2022) corroborates the order of magnitude. Subsequent Brazilian studies (Sobrinho et al. 2023; Andrade et al. 2024) report comparable estimates for the 2018-2022 period.
ground_truth_source: GBD 2019 Risk Factor Collaborators. Lancet 2020;396:1223–1249. https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(20)30752-2; WHO Air Pollution and Health 2022: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/ambient-(outdoor)-air-quality-and-health

prompt_rendered: List the three principal federal Brazilian programs for monitoring and controlling ambient air pollution in force in 2024. For each, provide: official acronym, year of creation, and the executing federal agency or ministry.
ground_truth: (1) PRONAR — Programa Nacional de Controle da Qualidade do Ar, established by CONAMA Resolution 5/1989, coordinated by IBAMA / MMA; (2) PROCONVE — Programa de Controle da Poluição do Ar por Veículos Automotores, established by CONAMA Resolution 18/1986, coordinated by IBAMA; (3) PROMOT — Programa de Controle da Poluição do Ar por Motociclos e similares, established by CONAMA Resolution 297/2002, coordinated by IBAMA.
ground_truth_source: MMA — Programa Nacional de Controle da Qualidade do Ar (PRONAR): https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/qualidade-ambiental/qualidade-do-ar; IBAMA — PROCONVE/PROMOT: https://www.gov.br/ibama/pt-br/assuntos/emissoes-e-residuos/emissoes/proconve-promot

prompt_rendered: A Brazilian metropolitan region is experiencing a forecast thermal-inversion episode with PM2.5 levels expected to exceed 75 µg/m³ in 24 hours. Recommend three short-term policy actions (deployable within 48 hours) to reduce population exposure and emissions during the episode. For each action, briefly justify with reference to public health evidence or operational feasibility.
ground_truth: Evidence-based short-term episode response actions include: (1) Issuance of public health advisory via municipal civil defense and health secretariat, recommending vulnerable populations (children, elderly, COPD/asthma patients, outdoor workers) to reduce outdoor activity — see WHO 2021 guidance on episode communication; (2) Activation of emergency vehicle restriction (e.g., expanded license-plate rotation, freight restriction in CBD) — proven 8-15% PM reduction in São Paulo Operação Inverno; (3) Temporary suspension of high-emission industrial sources subject to operational license clauses (e.g., open burning, asphalt plants). Rubric scores responses on: action specificity, public health linkage, operational feasibility, and use of authoritative sources.
ground_truth_source: Rubric-based evaluation (no single ground-truth answer); reference policies: CETESB Operação Inverno https://cetesb.sp.gov.br/ar/operacao-inverno/; WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines episode communication chapter.
